subject: Model Mosaic-Epsilon v3.2 — p99 latency containment & rollforward option
messages:
From: ops-alerts@redwood-monitoring.com
To: markus.klein@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2029-05-02T09:12:00Z
Subject: ALERT: mosaic-epsilon:v3.2 p99 latency > 1.6s (5m spike)

Alert details: automated detection triggered at 2029-05-02T09:11Z.
- Metric: request_latency.p99 (in ms)
- Baseline: 800ms
- Current: 1640ms
- Service: mosaic-epsilon
- Variant: v3.2 (canary ratio 40%)

Top affected routes: /generate, /chat/stream
Attached: grafana_p99_timeseries.png (screenshot), performance_snapshot_20290502.csv (sampling).

Immediate suggestion: reduce canary traffic to 0% or failover traffic to v3.1 while engineering investigates.

---
ops-alerts@redwood-monitoring.com
From: markus.klein@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2029-05-02T09:34:00Z
Subject: Re: ALERT: mosaic-epsilon:v3.2 p99 latency > 1.6s (5m spike)

Thanks for the ping. I pulled the Grafana snapshot — the p99 jump lines up with a new kernel rollout on a subset of hosts and coincides with a small increase in IO wait on those nodes.

Options on the table (short window):
- Immediate fallback to v3.1 (safe, known-good); 0% canary, route traffic to stable pool.
- Rollforward to v3.2.1 (hotfix build with patch for kernel affinity) — requires quick validation (15m) and a canary at 10% while we monitor.
- Keep v3.2 but throttle canary to 5% and enable KV cache-priming to reduce tail.

I recommend fallback to v3.1 for Mosaic (customer-impacting) unless we can run a quick v3.2.1 validation and get buy-in for a controlled rollforward. Need authorization on credits/communication to Mosaic and sign-off for a short SLA carveout window if we must do traffic surgery.

Can Product (Kim) and Eng (Neha) weigh in on risks for rollforward vs fallback? Ben — please prep a customer message variant for both outcomes (fallback vs rollforward).

-Markus
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: markus.klein@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2029-05-02T10:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Model Mosaic-Epsilon v3.2 — p99 latency containment & rollforward option

I concur with Markus: fallback to v3.1 is the least customer-risky move and minimizes exposure to additional regressions. Engineering notes:
- v3.2.1 hotfix is already built but not validated across IO-sensitive hosts; validation test suite is ~12 minutes plus smoke.
- If we opt for rollforward, we should start validation immediately and hold 20% capacity warm for quick cutover.

Customer comms: I suggest a short, honest note acknowledging we saw an atypical latency increase, that we're reverting to the known good variant while we complete a targeted fix, and offering a short credit for API token usage during the window if SLA thresholds are missed. Ben, draft two options: (1) immediate fallback notice, (2) rollforward-with-validation note.

Kim Park
Head of Product — Runtime
From: Rachel Lee <rachel.lee@mosaic.ai>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2029-05-02T12:18:00Z
Subject: Re: latency on /generate (Mosaic traffic)

Thanks for the heads-up — we started seeing slow responses in the morning and a few downstream retries. Our customer success team is getting inbound reports.

Priority for us: stability + a clear ETA to recovery. Mosaic is sensitive to tail latency for our SLAs (we're in EU but routing via us for short term).

Please let us know: will you be reverting to the prior variant or attempting a hotfix rollforward? ETA for either is critical so we can triage internally.

— Rachel
Ops Lead, Mosaic Analytics
From: markus.klein@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2029-05-02T14:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Model Mosaic-Epsilon v3.2 — p99 latency containment & rollforward option

Decision after quick sync with Eng: we will attempt a validated rollforward to v3.2.1 first. Plan:
- 14:10 UTC: start v3.2.1 validation on a staging cluster (12m).
- 14:30 UTC: promote v3.2.1 to 10% canary for Mosaic routes, monitor p99 for 30m.
- 15:00 UTC: if p99 drops to <=900ms, ramp to 60% and then to 100% over 45min.
- Fallback contingency: if p99 remains >1.2s at any checkpoint, immediately revert to v3.1 and notify Mosaic.

Ben: draft and send the rollforward-with-validation comms at 14:25 (include potential credit language). Naomi: prep a support bridge and patch notes.

I am also requesting a temporary SLA grace window authorization for Mosaic from leadership — the customer may request a credit depending on token counts during the incident. Please escalate for final sign-off.

-Markus
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: markus.klein@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2029-05-02T17:48:00Z
Subject: Re: Model Mosaic-Epsilon v3.2 — p99 latency containment & rollforward option

Final: leadership has approved a narrow SLA grace window for Mosaic (14:10–16:30 UTC) to allow the rollforward and validation. We also pre-authorized up to 5% account credit if we fail to meet p99 <=1.0s for more than 30 minutes during that window.

Action items completed:
- Rollforward validation executed and canary started at 14:30; p99 at 14:55 is 860ms (tracked in Grafana link).
- Continued ramp to 60% completed at 15:15, p99 stable ~890ms.
- Full promotion complete at 16:05; final monitoring window passed.

Closure: incident resolved by rollforward to v3.2.1. Naomi, please close the support bridge and log the incident with JIRA-RED-4521. Ben, send final customer note with credit wording and thank-you.

Kim Park
Head of Product — Runtime
